thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: realtime.p99 > 2.0s in us-west-2 for route /v1/generate (alert id: A-510555). Automatic detection triggered at 2026-03-15T10:02:00Z. Paging oncall.
Sam: ack, I'm on it. Which model/route variant is spiking?
Maya: I'm looking at the dashboard now — p95 looks stable but p99 jumps around 2–3s starting 10:02. Heatmap shows tail latency concentrated on streaming sessions for model gen-v2-quant.
Luis: quick check: any deploys or config changes around 09:58–10:02?
Maya: Deploy history shows a canary rollout of gen-v2-quant -> gen-v2-quant-canary at 09:58 (deploy id d-2026-03-15-0958). Could be correlated.
Sam: Can we get logs for streaming workers? run: `kubectl logs -n runtime streaming-worker --since=10m | tail -n 200`
Luis: pasted snippet:
```
[10:01:58] ERROR stream_write timeout=5000ms session=abcd1234
[10:02:03] WARN kvcache miss model=gen-v2-quant key=prefix:xyz
[10:02:05] ERROR backpressure: queue_depth=120 write_failures=6
```
Maya: seeing repeated "stream_write timeout" and backpressure warnings, plus kvcache misses. That would explain long tails vs median.
Toni: I'm on call, taking ownership. First things first: can we stop the canary traffic to confirm? If it's causal, rollback should reduce tail latency.
Sam: good call. I'll switch routing weight to 0 for the canary.
Sam: `redwood-route set-weight --route gen-v2-quant-canary --weight 0` executed. Route change acknowledged by DeployBot.
DeployBot: Route update applied: gen-v2-quant-canary weight -> 0 :white_check_mark:
Luis: watching metrics — p99 dropped from ~2.6s down to ~1.3s within 45s of route change. p95 steady at ~0.6–0.8s.
Maya: rollback helped but some sessions still show streaming stalls. Looks like the rollback removed the new traffic source but the runtime is still recovering (open sessions/backlog).
Sam: Two mitigations in parallel: (1) scale streaming workers by +4 replicas, (2) consider toggling kv cache write path to reduce misses for affected keyspace. Scaling is less risky — I'll scale first.
Sam: `kubectl scale deployment/streaming-worker -n runtime --replicas=12`
Luis: scale command applied. New pods starting; CPU spiky but stabilizing.
Maya: after scale, p95 ~0.55s, p99 ~0.95s and falling. Backpressure counters also dropping.
Toni: Good. I'm going to page SRE and keep this incident. Summary for handoff -> Eng SRE oncall (Toni):
- Timeline: spike began 2026-03-15T10:02Z
- Symptom: sustained p99 > 2s for /v1/generate streaming sessions; median unaffected
- Correlation: canary rollout d-2026-03-15-0958; logs show stream_write timeouts and kvcache misses
- Immediate mitigation: route weight set to 0 for canary (done), scaled streaming-worker replicas +4 (done)
- Current status: p95 0.55s, p99 0.95s and trending to baseline. No rolling errors in host health
- Customer impact: estimated ~1.6% of requests in the window experienced >2s tail latency; highest impact on a handful of high-throughput tenants (CustomerA, CustomerB). No data loss or corrupted responses observed.
ProductOps: flagged top customers and notified account reps (CustomerA rep notified). They reported increased error rates in telemetry but no customer calls yet.
Maya: next immediate actions for root cause: collect heap/profile from streaming-worker pods that experienced backpressure, gather KV cache miss rate histograms, and compare kernel/networking metrics for the node pool used by canary.
Sam: I'll create a short runbook entry for this: triggers (p99 > 2s for >2m), quick mitigations (rollback, scale, kv toggle), and metrics to watch (stream_write_errors, kvcache_miss_rate, queue_depth).
Toni: Taking ownership of the incident. I'll coordinate the postmortem and assign to runtime+deploy teams to debug canary behavior. Assigning owners: @Maya runtime, @Luis logs/monitoring, @Sam mitigations/runbook, @DeployTeam investigate canary artifact.
Sam: assigning a follow-up ticket: INC-510555-rootcause, linking logs + dashboard snapshots.
Maya: saving relevant graphs and adding them to the ticket; attaching `dashboard:realtime/tail-latency` snapshot.
Luis: a quick sanity check: `ss -tna | grep ESTAB | wc -l` on node showed an increase in established connections during spike — will include in notes.
incident-bot: Incident record updated: A-510555 -> status: acknowledged -> mitigated (initial). Pager updated.
Toni: I'll stay on this and postupdates in the incident channel. If p99 creeps back above 2s, I'll escalate to infra lead. For now, handoff accepted. :white_check_mark:
Sam: thanks all — great fast work. Leaving this thread for Toni to follow up with postmortem and timeline. Closing live mitigation window at 10:08Z, leaving follow-ups open.
ProductOps: Noted customer comms will wait until root cause determined; early heads-up sent.
Maya: adding a short note: consider adding a canary pre-check that runs a small streaming workload with kvcache stress to catch this class of regressions earlier.
Toni: acknowledged. I'll include that in remediation and the action items. Off to run a deeper profiling run now.
Sam: :thumbsup:
